item.problem_title: Variance estimation after cloning and sequence expansion has no scalable, correct default
item.problem_statement: Sequential emulation and cloning expand a dataset by orders of magnitude: a row per eligible decision point per person, multiplied by the strategies each person is initially compatible with. Two dependence structures result, repeated participation and clone-level copies of one history, and naive standard errors ignore both. Person-clustered sandwich inference handles both scalably when the weights are treated as fixed or the estimating-equation conditions hold, and for parametric marginal structural models with inverse probability weighting there are now evaluated alternatives with simulation guidance on coverage against cost. No default handles the harder case: clone-level dependence together with site clustering and the uncertainty from weights estimated by flexible nuisance models, at sequence-expansion scale. The bootstrap that would is correct in principle and prohibitive in practic

item.evidence: The bootstrap is the variance route the entry says is correct in principle and often prohibitive, and this replaces it with a synthetic multiple imputation variance estimator needing around 50 imputations and a smaller Monte Carlo sample. That is a scalable correct default for the g-formula, though not for the cloning and sequence expansion the entry is about, so it addresses the computational half of the problem in a neighbouring design.
item.quote: Moreover, it avoids the need to use bootstrapping for inference, which is particularly attractive in the context of combining MI for missing data with G-formula for causal inference.

item.problem_title: Code, phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not available for emulations
item.problem_statement: The TARGET statement asks for the target protocol, its data mapping, the estimands, the assumptions, the estimates and the sensitivity analyses, and is a transparency instrument rather than a risk-of-bias certification. An emulation is not externally auditable when its final analysis code, its complete versioned phenotype logic and its weight diagnostics are unavailable, and in current practice they are: most emulations are irreproducible in operative detail despite faithful protocol reporting. Where the real data cannot be shared, code plus a documented schema, a container and synthetic fixtures establishes that the pipeline executes and what it does; it does not reproduce the published estimate, and auditability rather than reproduction is what such a release can deliver. Material protocol amendments belong in a versioned decision log, which nothing currently requires.

item.problem_title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
item.problem_statement: Identifying a sustained-strategy effect requires consistency, sequential exchangeability and positivity, and the estimator families differ in which nuisance components they need. When those components are fitted by machine learning, the model that predicts treatment best is not the model that minimizes the finite-sample error of the causal estimator: a highly adaptive learner can achieve excellent discrimination while returning near-zero treatment probabilities, poor longitudinal balance and invalid inference. Balance-calibrated weight fitting exists and has been applied, so the field is not selecting on prediction alone. What is missing is a criterion that combines predictive risk with the estimator-specific diagnostics that matter, longitudinal balance, weight tails and the remainder-rate condition, in one selection rule, and a default library tuned that way rather than for prediction.

item.evidence: This addresses the nuisance-model half of the entry from a different direction: instead of a criterion for selecting among learners, it reduces what has to be modeled to one scalar per period, removing the factorisation choice. It also reports what flexible learners do and do not buy, citing simulations where singly robust g-formula estimators with machine learning did not improve on misspecified parametric models and both were improved by double machine learning or TMLE, and finding BART competitive only at later periods.

item.problem_title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
item.problem_statement: The available estimators differ in what they assume rather than only in how they perform. Active-comparator new-user designs with regression or propensity adjustment handle baseline initiation and not treatment-confounder feedback. Matching gives a transparent population, discards information, and often leaves its estimand unstated. Marginal structural models represent regime effects directly and are unstable under extreme weights. The parametric g-formula supports flexible estimands and is sensitive to sequential outcome-model misspecification. G-estimation avoids modeling the treatment-free outcome distribution and is technically demanding. Longitudinal targeted learning is doubly robust, computationally heavy and sensitive to practical positivity. No estimator is defensible as a universal default, and a study reporting one reports a number whose dependence on that choice is unknown: n

item.problem_title: Convergence of treatment in the comparator arm attenuates the observational intention-to-treat analogue with follow-up length
item.problem_statement: The observational analogue of an intention-to-treat effect contrasts assigning initiation now against not initiating now, and in that contrast the comparator group does not stay untreated: patients frequently initiate later. Reduced separation between the treatment histories can move the estimated effect at longer horizons, in a direction and by an amount that depend on the treatment-effect dynamics, the switching mechanism, the competing events and the effect scale. This is a feature of the estimand rather than a bias to be removed, and it occurs in randomized trials too. What emulations do not do is report it: the cumulative incidence of initiation in each arm over follow-up is rarely published, so a reader cannot judge how far the contrasted strategies stayed distinct, and a null result at a long horizon cannot be read against the convergence that actually occurred.
item.paper: Addressing treatment switching in the ALTA-1L trial with g-methods: exploring the impact of model specification
item.evidence: The entry's rewritten claim is that reduced separation between treatment histories moves the estimate by an amount that depends on the switching mechanism, and that this is not reported. Here it is quantified on a real trial: the intention-to-treat effect understates the benefit by 10 to 45 percentage points depending on method and specification. The direction and size are recovered only by re-analysis, which is the reporting gap the entry names.

verdicts.reason: A design-specific checklist that requires weight summaries, truncation reporting, natural-course checks, explicit assumptions, and transparent sensitivity results is a useful partial prototype of an assumption panel. It is not an adopted standard or a complete dashboard, and merely listing assumptions does not establish them.

item.problem_title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
item.problem_statement: Exchangeability and consistency cannot be established from observed data. Neither, strictly, can positivity, model correctness or phenotype validity: the available checks reveal or falsify particular problems and certify none of them. Current reports blur both distinctions. A propensity-score overlap plot is offered and the reader infers that the assumptions have been checked, when the plot is a partial diagnostic of one of them and silent on the rest. No standard panel exists, so what appears varies by author and by journal, and an absent diagnostic cannot be distinguished from one that was run and not reported. A single panel cannot be adequate for every design, which is a constraint on the solution rather than an argument against it.
item.paper: Addressing treatment switching in the ALTA-1L trial with g-methods: exploring the impact of model specification
item.evidence: The seven-step checklist is close to the assumption panel the entry asks for: report the weight distribution, report every truncation level, compare the natural course against the observed data, name the five assumptions both estimators share, and report divergent sensitivity results transparently. It is one paper's checklist for one design rather than an adopted standard, and it separates what can be inspected from what must be assumed.
